title.zh: 卷四十九 唐書25: 后妃列傳一
title.en: Volume 49 Book of Later Tang 25: Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts
title.raw: 卷四十九 唐書25: 后妃列傳一 Volume 49 Book of Later Tang 25: Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 武皇帝貞簡皇后曹氏，莊宗之母也，太原人，以良家子嬪於武皇。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenjian of Emperor Wu, Lady Cao, was the mother of Emperor Zhuangzong. A native of Taiyuan, she entered the harem of the Martial Emperor as a woman of good family.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenjian, née Cao, consort of Emperor Wu and mother of Emperor Zhuangzong, was a native of Taiyuan who entered Li Keyong's harem as a woman of respectable family.

sentences.zh: 姿質閑麗，性謙退而明辨，雅為秦國夫人所重。

translations.literal: Her bearing was graceful and beautiful, her nature modest and retiring yet clear-sighted, and she was greatly esteemed by the Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful and beautiful in appearance, modest and clear-minded by nature, she was held in high regard by the Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 常從容謂武皇曰：「妾觀曹姬非常婦人，王其厚待之。」

translations.literal: She often said calmly to the Martial Emperor, "Your servant observes that Lady Cao is no ordinary woman. Your Majesty should treat her generously."
translations.idiomatic: She would often say to Li Keyong in an easy tone, "I can see that Lady Cao is no ordinary woman. You would do well to treat her generously."

sentences.zh: 武皇多內寵，乾寧初，平燕薊，得李匡儔妻張氏，姿色絕代，嬖幸無雙。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor had many favorites within the palace. In the early Qianning era, when he pacified Yan and Ji, he obtained Zhang, wife of Li Kuangchou, whose beauty was unmatched in her age, and she enjoyed favor beyond all others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong kept many favorites in the inner palace. In the early Qianning era, after he pacified Yan and Ji, he took Li Kuangchou's wife Zhang into his household. Her beauty was unrivaled in her day, and no other consort enjoyed such exclusive favor.

sentences.zh: 時姬侍盈室，罕得進禦，唯太后恩顧不衰。

translations.literal: At that time consorts and attendants filled the chambers, and Lady Cao rarely gained access to the imperial bed, yet the Empress Dowager's gracious favor toward her never waned.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and attendants now filled the palace, and Lady Cao seldom gained access to the emperor's bedchamber, yet the empress dowager's favor toward her never diminished.

sentences.zh: 武皇性嚴急，左右有過，必峻於譴罰，無敢言者，唯太后從容救諫，即為解顏。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor's nature was stern and harsh. When those around him erred, he always punished severely, and none dared speak up. Only the Empress Dowager, calmly interceding and remonstrating, could soften his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was stern and quick to punish. When those around him transgressed, he dealt out harsh penalties and no one dared speak up—only the empress dowager, by calmly interceding and remonstrating, could soften his anger.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗載誕，體貌奇傑，武皇異而憐之，太后益寵貴，諸夫人鹹出其下，後亦恭勤內助，左右稱之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was born, his physique and appearance were extraordinary. The Martial Emperor marveled at him and cherished him. The Empress Dowager grew ever more favored and honored; all the other ladies ranked below her. She was also respectful and diligent in domestic support, and those around her praised her.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong was born, his bearing and appearance were remarkable. Li Keyong was struck by the child and doted on him. Lady Cao grew ever more favored and honored; the other consorts all ranked below her. She was also respectful and diligent in managing the household, and those around her praised her.

sentences.zh: 武皇薨，莊宗嗣晉王位，時李克寧、李存顥謀變，人情危懼。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor died, Emperor Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne of Prince of Jin. At that time Li Kening and Li Cunhao plotted rebellion, and popular sentiment was alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong died, Zhuangzong succeeded as Prince of Jin. Li Kening and Li Cunhao then plotted rebellion, and the court was gripped by fear.

sentences.zh: 太后召監軍張承業，指莊宗謂之曰：「先人把臂授公此兒，如聞外謀，欲孤付托，公等但置予母子有地，毋令乞食於汴，幸矣。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned the army supervisor Zhang Chengye, pointed to Emperor Zhuangzong, and said to him, "Our forebear clasped your arm and entrusted this child to you. If I hear of outside plots and wish to entrust him alone, you need only secure a place for me and my son—do not let us beg for food at Bian—and that would be fortune enough."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned army supervisor Zhang Chengye, pointed to Zhuangzong, and said, "Our forebear clasped your arm and entrusted this boy to you. If outsiders plot and I must rely on you alone, see only that my son and I have somewhere to live and are not reduced to begging at Bian—that will be fortune enough."

sentences.zh: 承業因誅存顥、克寧，以清內難。

translations.literal: Chengye thereupon executed Cunhao and Kening to settle the internal crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye executed Cunhao and Kening, clearing the internal threat.

sentences.zh: 莊宗善音律，喜伶人謔浪，太后常提耳誨之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was skilled in music and delighted in the jesting of actors. The Empress Dowager often pulled his ear to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was skilled in music and loved the coarse jesting of actors. The empress dowager often pulled his ear to warn him.

sentences.zh: 天祐七年，鎮、定求援，莊宗促命治兵，太后曰：「予齒漸衰，兒但不墜先人之業為幸矣，何事櫛風沐雨，離我晨昏！」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou, Zhen and Ding sought aid. Emperor Zhuangzong urgently ordered troops raised. The Empress Dowager said, "My teeth are gradually failing. If my son only does not let our forebears' enterprise fall, that is fortune enough. Why must he brave wind and rain and leave my morning and evening!"
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 7 Zhen and Ding sought help, and Zhuangzong urgently ordered mobilization. The empress dowager said, "I am growing old. If my son only keeps our forebears' enterprise from falling, that is fortune enough. Why must he brave wind and rain and leave my side morning and evening!"

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「稟先王遺旨，須滅仇讎。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said, "Following the late king's final charge, I must destroy our enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "Following my late father's final charge, I must destroy our enemy.

sentences.zh: 山東之事，機不可失。」

translations.literal: As for affairs in Shandong, the opportunity must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: As for Shandong, the opportunity must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 及發，太后餞於汾橋，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: When he set out, the Empress Dowager saw him off at Fen Bridge, so grief-stricken she could not contain herself.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out, the empress dowager saw him off at Fen Bridge, overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定趙、魏，駐於鄴城，每一歲之內，馳駕歸寧者數四，民士服其仁孝。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei and encamped at Ye. Within each year he raced his carriage home to pay respects several times, and the people and officials admired his benevolence and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei and encamped at Ye, he raced home to pay his respects several times each year, and the people admired his benevolence and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 太后初封晉國夫人，莊宗即位，命宰臣盧損奉冊書上皇太后尊號。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had first been enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Jin. When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he ordered chief minister Lu Sun to present the patent of enfeoffment and bestow the honored title of empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had first been enfeoffed as Lady of Jin. When Zhuangzong took the throne, he ordered chief minister Lu Sun to present the patent and bestow on her the title of empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 其年平定河南，西幸洛陽，令皇弟存渥、皇子繼岌就太原迎奉。

translations.literal: That year he pacified Henan and traveled west to Luoyang, ordering his younger brother Cunwo and the prince Jiji to go to Taiyuan to escort her.
translations.idiomatic: That year he pacified Henan and went west to Luoyang, sending his younger brother Cunwo and Prince Jiji to Taiyuan to escort her.

sentences.zh: 莊宗親至懷州，迎歸長壽宮，太后素與劉太妃善，分訣之後，悒然不樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong personally went as far as Huai Prefecture to welcome her back to Changshou Palace. The Empress Dowager had long been on good terms with Grand Consort Liu; after parting from her, she was depressed and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong went in person as far as Huaizhou to welcome her to Changshou Palace. The empress dowager had long been close to Grand Consort Liu, and after their parting she was despondent.

sentences.zh: 俄聞太妃寢疾，尚醫中使，問訊結轍。

translations.literal: Soon word came that the Grand Consort had taken to her bed with illness. Imperial physicians and inner envoys followed one another in inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the grand consort had fallen ill. Imperial physicians and inner envoys followed one another with inquiries.

sentences.zh: 既而謂莊宗曰：「吾與太妃恩如伯仲，彼經年抱疾，但見吾麵，差足慰心，吾暫至晉陽，旬朔與之俱來。」

translations.literal: She then said to Emperor Zhuangzong, "The Grand Consort and I are as close as elder and younger brother. She has been ill for years; if she could only see my face, that would be enough to comfort her heart. I shall go briefly to Jinyang and return with her within a month."
translations.idiomatic: She then told Zhuangzong, "The grand consort and I are as close as sisters. She has been ill for years; seeing my face would comfort her. I shall go briefly to Jinyang and return with her within a month."

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「時方暑毒，山路崎嶇，無煩往復，可令存渥輩迎侍太妃。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said, "The season is now fiercely hot and poisonous, and the mountain roads are rugged. Do not trouble yourself with the round trip. You may have Cunwo and the others go to attend the Grand Consort."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "The heat is fierce and the mountain roads are rugged. Do not trouble yourself with the journey. Let Cunwo and the others go to attend the grand consort."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: She thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: She desisted.

sentences.zh: 及凶問至，太后慟哭累旬，由是不豫，尋崩於長壽宮。

translations.literal: When news of the death arrived, the Empress Dowager wailed in grief for many days. Thereafter she was unwell and soon died in Changshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the death arrived, the empress dowager mourned for many days, fell ill, and soon died in Changshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 同光三年冬十月，上諡曰貞簡皇太后，葬於壽安陵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the third year of Tongguang, she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Zhenjian and buried at Shou'an Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in Tongguang 3 she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Zhenjian and buried at Shou'an Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 太妃劉氏，武皇之正室也。

translations.literal: Imperial Grand Consort Liu was the Martial Emperor's principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Grand Consort Liu was Li Keyong's principal wife.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《劉太妃傳》，原本闕佚。

translations.literal: (Note: The biography of Grand Consort Liu is missing from the original text.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Grand Consort Liu is missing from the original text.

sentences.zh: 考《北夢瑣言》云：晉王李克用妻劉夫人，常隨軍行，至於軍機，多所宏益。

translations.literal: Examining the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》, it says: Liu, wife of Prince of Jin Li Keyong, often accompanied the army on campaign and contributed greatly to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: According to the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》, Liu, wife of Li Keyong, Prince of Jin, often accompanied the army on campaign and contributed greatly to military affairs.

sentences.zh: 先是，汴州上源驛有變，晉王憤恨，欲回軍攻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, there had been an incident at Shangyuan Post Station in Bian Prefecture. The Prince of Jin, filled with anger and resentment, wished to turn the army back and attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the incident at Shangyuan Post Station in Bianzhou, Li Keyong, filled with anger, wanted to turn the army around and attack the city.

sentences.zh: 夫人曰：「公為國討賊，而以杯酒私忿，必若攻城，即曲在於我。

translations.literal: Lady Liu said, "Your Lordship is campaigning for the state to suppress rebels, yet because of a private grudge over a cup of wine, if you insist on attacking the city, the wrong will be on our side.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu said, "You are campaigning on behalf of the state to suppress rebels. To turn back over a private grudge about a cup of wine—if you insist on attacking the city, the wrong will be on our side.

sentences.zh: 不如回師，自有朝廷可以論列。」

translations.literal: It would be better to withdraw the army. There is still the court through which the matter can be laid out."
translations.idiomatic: Better to withdraw the army. The court still exists, and the matter can be laid before it."

sentences.zh: 於是班退。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army withdrew in formation.
translations.idiomatic: The army thereupon withdrew in formation.

sentences.zh: 天復中，周德威為汴軍所敗，三軍潰散，汴軍乘我，晉王危懼，與李存信議，欲出保雲州。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era, Zhou Dewei was defeated by the Bian army. The three armies scattered in rout. The Bian army pressed the advantage against us. The Prince of Jin was alarmed and in fear, and together with Li Cunxin discussed abandoning the city to hold Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era, Zhou Dewei was defeated by the Bian army and the three armies broke and scattered. As the Bian forces pressed their advantage, Li Keyong was alarmed and, together with Li Cunxin, discussed abandoning their position and retreating to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 夫人曰：「存信本北方牧羊兒也，焉顧成敗！

translations.literal: Lady Liu said, "Cunxin was originally a shepherd boy of the northern frontier. What does he care about success or failure!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu said, "Cunxin was originally a shepherd boy from the northern frontier. What does he care whether we succeed or fail!

sentences.zh: 王常笑王行瑜棄城失勢，被人屠割，今復欲效之，何也？

translations.literal: Your Majesty often laughed at Wang Xingyu for abandoning his city, losing his power, and being slaughtered by others. Now you wish to imitate him again—why?
translations.idiomatic: You often mocked Wang Xingyu for abandoning his city, losing his power, and being cut down by others. Why do you now want to do the same?

sentences.zh: 王頃歲避難塞外，幾遭陷害，賴遇朝廷多事，方得復歸。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, in recent years, took refuge beyond the frontier and nearly came to harm. Only because the court was beset by many troubles were you able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few years ago you took refuge beyond the frontier and nearly came to harm. You were able to return only because the court was beset by turmoil.

sentences.zh: 今一旦出城，便有不測之變，焉能遠及！」

translations.literal: Now, if you leave the city at once, unforeseen disaster will follow. How could you reach far!"
translations.idiomatic: If you leave the city now, unforeseen disaster will follow at once. You would never get far!"

sentences.zh: 晉王止行。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin stopped the move.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 居數日，亡散之士復集，軍城安定，夫人之力也。

translations.literal: After several days, the soldiers who had fled and scattered gathered again, and the garrison city was stabilized—this was Lady Liu's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the scattered troops reassembled and the garrison city was stabilized—thanks to Lady Liu.

sentences.zh: 《五代會要》云：同光元年四月，冊為皇太妃。

translations.literal: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 says: In the fourth month of the first year of Tongguang, she was enfeoffed as Imperial Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that in the fourth month of the first year of Tongguang she was enfeoffed as imperial grand consort.

sentences.zh: 《歐陽史》云：莊宗即位，冊尊曹氏為皇太后，而以嫡母劉氏為皇太妃。

translations.literal: The 《History of Ouyang》 says: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he enfeoffed and honored Lady Cao as Empress Dowager, while his principal mother Lady Liu was made Imperial Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of Ouyang》 records that when Zhuangzong took the throne, he enfeoffed Lady Cao as empress dowager and made his principal mother Lady Liu imperial grand consort.

sentences.zh: 太妃往謝太后，太后有慚色。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort went to thank the Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: The grand consort went to thank the empress dowager, who looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 太妃曰：「願吾兒享國無窮，使吾獲沒於地以從先君幸矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort said, "I only wish that my son may enjoy the realm without end, so that I may die and follow my late lord—that would be fortune enough.
translations.idiomatic: The grand consort said, "I only wish that my son may reign forever. If I can die and follow my late lord, that will be fortune enough for me.

sentences.zh: 復何言哉！」

translations.literal: What more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: What more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁入洛，使人迎太后歸洛，居長壽宮，而太妃獨留晉陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and entered Luoyang, he sent men to welcome the Empress Dowager back to Luoyang, where she resided in Changshou Palace, while the Grand Consort alone remained in Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and entered Luoyang, he sent men to bring the empress dowager to Luoyang, where she took up residence in Changshou Palace, while the grand consort alone remained in Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 同光三年五月，太妃薨。）〉

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Tongguang, the Grand Consort died.)〉
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Tongguang, the grand consort died.)〉

sentences.zh: 魏國夫人陳氏，襄州人，本昭宗之宮嬪也。

translations.literal: Lady Chen, Lady of the State of Wei, was a native of Xiang Prefecture and had originally been a palace consort of Emperor Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen, Lady of Wei, was a native of Xiangzhou and had originally been a palace consort of Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，武皇奉詔討王行瑜，駐軍於渭北，昭宗降朱書御劄，出陳氏及內妓四人以賜武皇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning, the Martial Emperor received orders to campaign against Wang Xingyu and encamped north of the Wei River. Emperor Zhaozong issued an imperial letter in vermilion and sent out Lady Chen and four inner courtesans to bestow upon the Martial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 2 Li Keyong received orders to campaign against Wang Xingyu and encamped north of the Wei. Emperor Zhaozong issued an imperial letter in vermilion and sent Lady Chen and four inner courtesans to bestow upon him.

sentences.zh: 陳氏素知書，有才貌，武皇深加寵重。

translations.literal: Lady Chen was versed in writing and gifted in talent and appearance. The Martial Emperor greatly favored and honored her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen was literate and gifted in talent and beauty. Li Keyong greatly favored her.

sentences.zh: 及光化之後，時事多難，武皇常獨居深念，嬪媵鮮得侍謁，唯陳氏得召見。

translations.literal: After the Guanghua era, the times were full of hardship. The Martial Emperor often sat alone in deep thought; consorts and attendants rarely gained audience, and only Lady Chen was summoned to see him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guanghua era, when the times were troubled, Li Keyong often sat alone in deep thought. Consorts and attendants rarely saw him; only Lady Chen was summoned.

sentences.zh: 陳氏性既靜退，不以寵侍自侈，武皇常呼為阿者。

translations.literal: Lady Chen's nature was calm and retiring, and she did not grow arrogant from favor and attendance. The Martial Emperor often called her A-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Calm and retiring by nature, Lady Chen did not grow arrogant from favor. Li Keyong often called her A-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 及武皇大漸之際，陳氏侍醫藥，垂泣言：「妾為王執掃除之役，十有四年矣，王萬一不幸，妾將何托！

translations.literal: As the Martial Emperor drew near his end, Lady Chen attended his medicines and weeping said, "Your servant has performed sweeping and cleaning duties for Your Majesty for fourteen years. If Your Majesty should meet misfortune, whom shall your servant rely upon!
translations.idiomatic: As Li Keyong lay dying, Lady Chen attended his medicines and wept, "I have served you in sweeping and cleaning for fourteen years. If misfortune should befall you, whom shall I rely upon!

sentences.zh: 既不能以身為殉，願落發為尼，為王讀一藏佛經，以報平昔。」

translations.literal: Since I cannot follow you in death, I wish to shave my head and become a nun, to read one complete Buddhist canon for Your Majesty and repay our former days."
translations.idiomatic: Since I cannot die with you, I wish to shave my head and become a nun and read the complete Buddhist canon for you, to repay our former days."

sentences.zh: 武皇為之流涕。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor wept for her.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong wept at her words.

sentences.zh: 及武皇薨，陳氏果落發持經，法名智願，後居於洛陽佛寺，莊宗賜號建法大師。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor died, Lady Chen indeed shaved her head and upheld the sutras. Her dharma name was Zhiyuan. Later she resided in a Buddhist monastery in Luoyang, and Emperor Zhuangzong granted her the title Great Master Jianfa.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong died, Lady Chen shaved her head and took up the sutras under the dharma name Zhiyuan. She later lived in a Luoyang monastery, and Zhuangzong granted her the title Great Master Jianfa.

sentences.zh: 天成中，明帝幸其院，改賜圓惠大師。

translations.literal: During the Tiancheng era, Emperor Ming visited her monastery and changed her grant to Great Master Yuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era Mingzong visited her monastery and changed her title to Great Master Yuanhui.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，卒於太原。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin she died at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: She died at Taiyuan during the Jin Tianfu era.

sentences.zh: 追諡光國大師，塔以惠寂為名也。

translations.literal: She was posthumously honored as Great Master Guangguo, and her pagoda was named Huiji.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously honored as Great Master Guangguo, and her pagoda was named Huiji.

sentences.zh: 莊宗神閔敬皇后劉氏。

translations.literal: Empress Shenminjing Liu of Emperor Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shenminjing Liu, consort of Emperor Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《劉後傳》，原本闕佚。

translations.literal: (Note: The biography of Empress Liu is missing from the original text.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Empress Liu is missing from the original text.

sentences.zh: 考《北夢瑣言》云：莊宗劉皇后，魏州成安人，家世寒微。

translations.literal: Examining the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》, it says: Empress Liu of Emperor Zhuangzong was a native of Cheng'an in Weizhou, from a humble family.
translations.idiomatic: According to the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》, Empress Liu of Zhuangzong was a native of Cheng'an in Weizhou from a humble family.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻魏州，取成安，得後，時年五六歲。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Weizhou and took Cheng'an, he obtained the future empress, who was then five or six years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong attacked Weizhou and took Cheng'an, he obtained the future empress, who was then five or six years old.

sentences.zh: 歸晉陽宮，為太后侍者，教吹笙。

translations.literal: She was brought to the palace at Jinyang, where she served the Empress Dowager and was taught to play the sheng.
translations.idiomatic: She was brought to the Jinyang palace, where she served the empress dowager and was taught to play the sheng.

sentences.zh: 及笄，姿色絕眾，聲伎亦所長。

translations.literal: When she came of age, her beauty surpassed all others, and she was also skilled in music and performance.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age, her beauty surpassed all others, and she was also accomplished in music and performance.

sentences.zh: 太后賜莊宗，為韓國夫人侍者。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager bestowed her upon Emperor Zhuangzong as an attendant to the Lady of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager gave her to Zhuangzong as an attendant to the Lady of Han.

sentences.zh: 後誕皇子繼岌，寵待日隆。

translations.literal: Later she bore the prince Jiji, and her favor and treatment grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Later she bore the prince Li Jiji, and her favor grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 他日，成安人劉叟詣鄴宮見上，稱夫人之父。

translations.literal: One day Liu Sou, a man of Cheng'an, came to the palace at Ye to see the emperor and claimed to be the lady's father.
translations.idiomatic: One day a man of Cheng'an named Liu Sou came to the Ye palace to see the emperor and claimed to be the empress's father.

sentences.zh: 有內臣劉建豐認之，即昔日黃須丈人，後之父也。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Liu Jianfeng recognized him as the yellow-bearded old man of former days—he was indeed the empress's father.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Liu Jianfeng recognized him as the yellow-bearded old man of former days—he was indeed the empress's father.

sentences.zh: 劉氏方與嫡夫人爭寵，皆以門族誇尚，劉氏恥為寒家，白莊宗曰：「妾去鄉之時，妾父死於亂兵，是時環屍而哭。

translations.literal: Lady Liu was then contending for favor with the principal wife, each boasting of her family status. Lady Liu was ashamed of her humble origins and told Emperor Zhuangzong, "When your servant left her home district, my father died at the hands of disorderly soldiers. At that time I wept over his body where it lay.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was then contending for favor with the principal wife, each boasting of her family status. Ashamed of her humble origins, she told Zhuangzong, "When I left my home district, my father was killed by disorderly soldiers. I wept over his body where it lay.

sentences.zh: 妾固無父，是何田舍翁詐偽及此！」

translations.literal: Your servant truly has no father. What rustic old man is this, to deceive to such a degree!"
translations.idiomatic: I truly have no father. What rustic old man is this, to deceive us so brazenly!"

sentences.zh: 乃於宮門笞之，其實後即叟之長女也。

translations.literal: She then had him flogged at the palace gate. In truth the empress was the old man's eldest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: She then had him flogged at the palace gate. In truth the empress was the old man's eldest daughter.

sentences.zh: 莊宗好俳優，宮中暇日，自負蓍囊藥篋，令繼岌相隨，以後父劉叟以醫卜為業也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong loved actors. On idle days in the palace, he would carry on his back a bag of divining stalks and a case of medicines, with Jiji following along, impersonating the empress's father Liu Sou, who made his living by medicine and divination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong loved actors. On idle days in the palace he would carry a diviner's bag and medicine case on his back, with Jiji following along, impersonating the empress's father Liu Sou, who made his living as a physician and diviner.

sentences.zh: 後方晝眠，及造其臥內，自稱劉衙推訪女，後大恚，笞繼岌。

translations.literal: The empress was napping by day when he entered her sleeping chamber, calling himself Magistrate Liu come to visit his daughter. The empress was greatly enraged and had Jiji flogged.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was napping when he entered her bedchamber, calling himself Magistrate Liu come to visit his daughter. She was furious and had Jiji flogged.

sentences.zh: 然為太后不禮，復以韓夫人居正，無以發明。

translations.literal: Yet because the Empress Dowager showed her no courtesy, and because the Lady of Han held the position of principal wife, there was no way to make the matter public.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because the empress dowager showed her no courtesy, and because the Lady of Han held the position of principal wife, there was no way to make the matter public.

sentences.zh: 大臣希旨請冊劉氏為皇后，議者以後出於寒賤，好興利聚財，初在鄴都，令人設法稗販，所鬻樵蘇果茹亦以皇后為名。

translations.literal: Ministers, seeking to please him, requested that Lady Liu be enfeoffed as empress. Critics noted that the empress came from humble and low origins and loved to pursue profit and amass wealth. When she was first at Ye, she had people set up schemes for petty trade, and even the firewood, kindling, fruit, and vegetables they sold were marketed under the empress's name.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, seeking to please him, requested that Lady Liu be enfeoffed as empress. Critics noted that she came from humble origins and loved to pursue profit and amass wealth. When she was first at Ye, she had people set up petty trading schemes, and even the firewood, kindling, fruit, and vegetables they sold were marketed under the empress's name.

sentences.zh: 正位之後，凡貢奉先入後宮，惟寫佛經施尼師，他無所賜，闕下諸軍困乏，以至妻子饑殍，宰相請出內庫俵給，後將出妝具銀盆兩口、皇子滿喜等三人，令鬻以贍軍。

translations.literal: After she took the principal position, all tribute first entered the inner palace. She gave only copied Buddhist scriptures to Buddhist nuns and bestowed nothing else. The armies at the capital were destitute, so that wives and children starved to death. The chief ministers requested that the inner treasury be opened for distribution, but the empress produced only two silver basins from her toilet set and the three princes Manxi and others, ordering them sold to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: After she took the throne as empress, all tribute first entered the inner palace. She gave only copied Buddhist scriptures to Buddhist nuns and bestowed nothing else. The armies at the capital were destitute, and wives and children starved to death. The chief ministers requested that the inner treasury be opened for distribution, but the empress produced only two silver basins from her toilet set and the three princes Manxi and others, ordering them sold to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 一旦作亂，亡國滅族，與夫褒姒、妲己無異也。

translations.literal: In the end she brought rebellion, the destruction of the state, and the extinction of her clan—no different from Baosi and Daji.
translations.idiomatic: In the end she brought rebellion, the destruction of the state, and the extinction of her clan—no different from Baosi and Daji.

sentences.zh: 先是，莊宗自為俳優，名曰李天下，雜於塗粉優雜之間，時為諸優撲扶摑搭，竟為嚚婦惡伶之傾玷，有國者得不以為前鑒！

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Zhuangzong himself acted as a performer under the name Li Tianxia, mingling among painted actors and variety players. At times the other performers would wrestle, support, slap, and strike him. In the end he was brought down by a wicked woman and vile actors—should not rulers take this as a warning!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhuangzong himself performed as an actor under the name Li Tianxia, mingling among painted players and variety performers. At times the other actors would wrestle with him, support him, slap him, and strike him. In the end he was brought down by a wicked woman and vile actors—should not rulers take this as a warning!

sentences.zh: 劉氏以囊盛金合犀帶四，欲於太原造寺為尼，沿路復通皇弟存渥，同簀而寢，明宗聞其穢，即令自殺。

translations.literal: Lady Liu, with a bag holding four gold boxes and rhinoceros-horn belts, wished to build a temple at Taiyuan and become a nun. Along the way she again had relations with the emperor's younger brother Cunwo and slept with him under one mat. When Emperor Mingzong heard of her debauchery, he immediately ordered her to kill herself.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, carrying a bag with four gold boxes and rhinoceros-horn belts, planned to build a temple at Taiyuan and become a nun. Along the way she again took up with the emperor's younger brother Cunwo and slept with him under one mat. When Mingzong heard of her debauchery, he ordered her to kill herself.

sentences.zh: 考《歐陽史》，作裨將袁建豐得後，納之晉宮，而《北夢瑣言》作內臣劉建豐，亦傳聞之異辭也。）〉

translations.literal: Examining the 《History of Ouyang》, it has the adjutant Yuan Jianfeng obtaining the future empress and bringing her into the Jin palace, while the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》 has the inner attendant Liu Jianfeng—these are differing accounts from hearsay.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of Ouyang》 names the adjutant Yuan Jianfeng as the one who obtained the future empress and brought her into the Jin palace, while the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》 names the inner attendant Liu Jianfeng—these are differing hearsay accounts.)〉

sentences.zh: 淑妃韓氏，莊宗正室。

translations.literal: Pure Consort Han was Emperor Zhuangzong's principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Pure Consort Han was Zhuangzong's principal wife.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《韓淑妃傳》，原本闕佚。

translations.literal: (Note: The biography of Pure Consort Han is missing from the original text.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Pure Consort Han is missing from the original text.

sentences.zh: 考《五代會要》云：同光二年十二月冊，以宰臣豆盧革、韋說為冊使，出應天門，登路車，鹵簿鼓吹前導，至於永福門降車，入右銀台門，至淑妃宮，受冊於內，文武百官立班稱賀。）〉

translations.literal: Examining the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》, it says: In the twelfth month of the second year of Tongguang she was enfeoffed. Chief ministers Dou Luge and Wei Shuo served as enfeoffment commissioners. They went out through Yingtian Gate, mounted the road chariot, with guards and musicians leading the way, descended at Yongfu Gate, entered through the Right Yintai Gate, proceeded to Pure Consort Han's palace, and received the patent of enfeoffment within. Civil and military officials stood in formation to offer congratulations.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that in the twelfth month of Tongguang 2 she was enfeoffed, with chief ministers Dou Luge and Wei Shuo as commissioners. They went out Yingtian Gate, mounted the road chariot with guards and musicians leading, descended at Yongfu Gate, entered through the Right Yintai Gate, proceeded to Pure Consort Han's palace, and received the patent within while civil and military officials stood in formation to congratulate her.)〉

sentences.zh: 德妃伊氏，莊宗次室。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Yi was Emperor Zhuangzong's second wife.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Yi was Zhuangzong's second wife.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《伊德妃傳》，原本闕佚。

translations.literal: (Note: The biography of Virtuous Consort Yi is missing from the original text.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Virtuous Consort Yi is missing from the original text.

sentences.zh: 考《北夢瑣言》云：莊宗皇帝嫡夫人韓氏，後為淑妃，伊氏為德妃。

translations.literal: Examining the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》, it says: Emperor Zhuangzong's principal wife Lady Han later became Pure Consort, and Lady Yi became Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: According to the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》, Zhuangzong's principal wife Lady Han later became pure consort, and Lady Yi became virtuous consort.

sentences.zh: 又言夫人夏氏，後嫁李讚華，所謂東丹王，即阿保機長子，性酷毒，侍婢微過，即以刀刲火灼。

translations.literal: It also mentions Lady Xia, who later married Li Zanhua—the so-called Prince of Dongdan, eldest son of Abaoji—who was cruel and vicious; for the slightest fault of a serving maid he would cut with a knife or burn with fire.
translations.idiomatic: It also mentions Lady Xia, who later married Li Zanhua—the so-called Prince of Dongdan, eldest son of Abaoji—who was cruel and vicious; for the slightest fault of a serving maid he would cut her with a knife or burn her with fire.

sentences.zh: 夏氏少長宮掖，不忍其凶，求離婚，歸河陽節度使夏魯奇家，後為尼也。

translations.literal: Lady Xia had grown up in the palace and could not bear his cruelty. She sought divorce and returned to the household of Xia Luqi, military governor of Heyang, and later became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xia had grown up in the palace and could not bear his cruelty. She sought a divorce and returned to the household of Xia Luqi, military governor of Heyang, and later became a nun.

sentences.zh: 《歐陽史·家人傳》：明宗立，悉放莊宗時宮人。

translations.literal: The 《History of Ouyang》, Biographies of the Imperial Family: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he released all the palace women from Emperor Zhuangzong's time.
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of Ouyang》, Biographies of the Imperial Family, records that when Mingzong took the throne, he released all the palace women from Zhuangzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 虢國夫人夏氏，歸夏魯奇家，後賜李讚華。

translations.literal: Lady Xia, Lady of the State of Guo, returned to Xia Luqi's household and was later bestowed upon Li Zanhua.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xia, Lady of the State of Guo, returned to Xia Luqi's household and was later bestowed upon Li Zanhua.

sentences.zh: 與《北夢瑣言》微異。

translations.literal: This differs slightly from the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》.
translations.idiomatic: This differs slightly from the 《Miscellaneous Notes from Northern Dreams》.

sentences.zh: 《遼史》又以夏氏為莊宗皇后，疑誤。

translations.literal: The 《History of Liao》 also treats Lady Xia as Empress of Emperor Zhuangzong, which is probably an error.
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of Liao》 also treats Lady Xia as Zhuangzong's empress, which is probably an error.

sentences.zh: 又案《五代會要》：莊宗朝內職，又有昭儀侯氏封汧國夫人，昭媛白氏封沂國夫人，出使美宣鄧氏封珝國夫人，禦正楚真張氏封涼國夫人，司簿德美周氏封宋國夫人，侍真吳氏封延陵郡夫人，懿才王氏封太原郡夫人，鹹一韓氏封昌黎郡夫人，瑤芳張氏封清河郡夫人，懿德王氏封琅琊郡夫人，宣一馬氏封扶風郡夫人，並同光二年十一月敕。）〉

translations.literal: Further examining the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》: Inner palace offices under Emperor Zhuangzong also included Palace Lady of Bright Deportment Hou, enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Qian; Palace Lady of Bright Charm Bai, enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Yi; Palace Lady of Envoy Beauty Xuan Deng, enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Xu; Palace Lady of Correct Deportment Chuzhen Zhang, enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Liang; Palace Secretary Demei Zhou, enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Song; Attendant Zhen Wu, enfeoffed as Lady of Yanling Commandery; Talented Lady Yi Wang, enfeoffed as Lady of Taiyuan Commandery; Xianyi Han, enfeoffed as Lady of Changli Commandery; Yaofang Zhang, enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe Commandery; Virtuous Lady Yi Wang, enfeoffed as Lady of Langya Commandery; Xuanyi Ma, enfeoffed as Lady of Fufeng Commandery—all by edict in the eleventh month of the second year of Tongguang.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 also lists inner palace offices under Zhuangzong: Palace Lady of Bright Deportment Hou as Lady of Qian; Palace Lady of Bright Charm Bai as Lady of Yi; Palace Lady of Envoy Beauty Xuan Deng as Lady of Xu; Palace Lady of Correct Deportment Chuzhen Zhang as Lady of Liang; Palace Secretary Demei Zhou as Lady of Song; Attendant Zhen Wu as Lady of Yanling Commandery; Talented Lady Yi Wang as Lady of Taiyuan Commandery; Xianyi Han as Lady of Changli Commandery; Yaofang Zhang as Lady of Qinghe Commandery; Virtuous Lady Yi Wang as Lady of Langya Commandery; Xuanyi Ma as Lady of Fufeng Commandery—all by edict in the eleventh month of Tongguang 2.)〉

sentences.zh: 明宗昭懿皇后夏氏，生秦王從榮及閔帝。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaoyi Xia of Emperor Mingzong bore the Prince of Qin Congrong and the Min Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaoyi Xia, consort of Mingzong, bore the Prince of Qin Congrong and the Min Emperor.

sentences.zh: 同光初，後以疾崩，明宗即位，追封為晉國夫人。

translations.literal: In the early Tongguang era the empress died of illness. When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongguang era she died of illness. When Mingzong took the throne, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Jin.

sentences.zh: 長興中，明宗以秦、宋二王位望既隆，因思從貴之義，乃下製曰：「故晉國夫人夏氏，素推仁德，久睦宗親，嘗施內助之方，不見中興之盛，予當御極，子並為王，有鵲巢之高，無翬衣之貴，貞魂永逝，懿範常存，考本朝之文，沿追冊之制，將慰懷於九族，冀葉慶於四星。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era, because the rank and prestige of the Princes of Qin and Song had already risen, Emperor Mingzong, reflecting on the principle of honoring one's mother, issued an edict saying, "The late Lady of the State of Jin, Lady Xia, always promoted benevolence and virtue and long kept kin harmonious. She once applied the ways of inner support, yet did not see the splendor of restoration. When I took the throne and my sons were all made princes, she had the height of the magpie's nest yet not the honor of the pheasant robe. Her chaste soul has passed forever, but her excellent example endures. Examining the texts of our dynasty and following the institutions of posthumous enfeoffment, I shall comfort the hearts of the nine clans and hope to bring blessing to the four stars.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changxing era, as the Princes of Qin and Song had risen in rank and prestige, Mingzong, reflecting on the duty of honoring one's mother, issued an edict: "The late Lady of Jin, Lady Xia, always promoted benevolence and long kept kin harmonious. She aided from within yet did not live to see restoration. When I took the throne and my sons were made princes, she had the magpie's nest yet not the pheasant robe. Her chaste soul has passed, but her excellent example endures. Following our dynasty's texts and the institutions of posthumous enfeoffment, I shall comfort the nine clans and hope to bring blessing to the four stars.

sentences.zh: 宜追冊為皇后，兼定懿號。」

translations.literal: She should be posthumously enfeoffed as empress, and her excellent honorific title should be fixed."
translations.idiomatic: She should be posthumously enfeoffed as empress, and her excellent honorific title should be fixed."

sentences.zh: 既而有司上諡曰昭懿。

translations.literal: Thereupon the responsible offices submitted the posthumous title Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 和武顯皇后曹氏。

translations.literal: Empress Hewuxian Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hewuxian Cao.

sentences.zh: （案：《曹後傳》，原本闕佚。

translations.literal: (Note: The biography of Empress Cao is missing from the original text.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Empress Cao is missing from the original text.

sentences.zh: 考《五代會要》云：天成三年正月，冊為淑妃，長興元年五月十四日，冊為皇后；

translations.literal: Examining the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》, it says: In the first month of the third year of Tiancheng she was enfeoffed as pure consort; on the fourteenth day of the fifth month of the first year of Changxing she was enfeoffed as empress;
translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that in the first month of Tiancheng 3 she was enfeoffed as pure consort, and on the fourteenth day of the fifth month of Changxing 1 as empress;

sentences.zh: 應順元年閏正月，冊為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the first year of Yingshun she was enfeoffed as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of Yingshun 1 she was enfeoffed as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 至清泰三年閏十一月，隨末帝崩於後樓。

translations.literal: By the intercalary eleventh month of the third year of Qingtai she perished with the Last Emperor at the Rear Tower.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of Qingtai 3 she perished with the Last Emperor at the Rear Tower.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖使人護葬，至天福五年正月二十八日，追冊曰和武顯皇后。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor of Jin sent men to escort the burial. On the twenty-eighth day of the first month of the fifth year of Tianfu she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Hewuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Jin sent men to escort the burial. On the twenty-eighth day of the first month of Tianfu 5 she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Hewuxian.

sentences.zh: 宣憲皇后魏氏。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanxian Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanxian Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《魏後傳》原本闕佚。

translations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Empress Wei is missing from the original text.

sentences.zh: 據《通鑒考異》引《唐廢帝實錄》云：宣憲皇后魏氏，鎮州平山人。

translations.literal: According to the 《Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror》, citing the 《Veritable Records of the Deposed Emperor of Tang》: Empress Xuanxian Wei was a native of Pingshan in Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror》, citing the 《Veritable Records of the Deposed Emperor of Tang》, records that Empress Xuanxian Wei was a native of Pingshan in Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 中和末，明宗徇地山東，留戍平山，得魏後。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhonghe era, Emperor Mingzong campaigned in Shandong, garrisoned Pingshan, and obtained the future Empress Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhonghe era, Mingzong campaigned in Shandong, garrisoned Pingshan, and obtained the future Empress Wei.

sentences.zh: 又云：明宗為裨將，性闊達，不能治生，曹後亦疏於畫略，生計所資，惟宣憲而已。

translations.literal: It also says: When Emperor Mingzong was an adjutant, his nature was open and easygoing and he could not manage livelihood. Empress Cao was also negligent in household planning. The support for their livelihood depended solely on Xuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: It also says that when Mingzong was a junior officer, he was open and easygoing and could not manage the household economy; Empress Cao was also negligent in such matters. Their livelihood depended solely on Xuanxian.

sentences.zh: 《五代會要》云：初封魯國太夫人，清泰二年二月，中書門下奏：「臣聞漢昭帝承祚禦曆，奉尊諡於雲陽；

translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that she was first enfeoffed as grand lady of the state of Lu. In the second month of Qingtai 2, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "We have heard that when Emperor Zhao of Han succeeded to the throne, he honored his mother with a posthumous title at Yunyang;

sentences.zh: 魏明帝繼體守文，思外家於甄館，而皆追崇微號，祔饗廟庭，克隆敬本之文，式葉愛親之道。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei succeeded and maintained the institutions, thinking of his mother's family at the Zhen Pavilion, and both pursued posthumous honor with modest titles and enshrined them in the ancestral temple, emulating the text of revering one's roots and fulfilling the way of loving one's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei succeeded and maintained the institutions, honoring his mother's family at the Zhen Pavilion; both pursued posthumous titles and enshrined them in the ancestral temple, emulating the principle of revering one's roots and fulfilling the duty of loving one's kin.

sentences.zh: 臣等又覽國史，竊見宗皇帝母曰昭成皇后竇氏，代宗皇帝母曰章敬太后吳氏，始嬪朱邸，俄幽宮，鴻圖既屬於明君，尊號鹹追於聖母。

translations.literal: Your servants have also reviewed the national histories and privately observe that the mother of Emperor Zong was Empress Zhaocheng Dou, and the mother of Emperor Daizong was Empress Dowager Zhangjing Wu. They first entered the princely residence as consorts and soon were confined in the palace. Once the great enterprise fell to enlightened rulers, honored titles were all posthumously conferred upon the holy mothers.
translations.idiomatic: We have also reviewed the national histories and observe that the mother of Emperor Xuanzong was Empress Zhaocheng Dou, and the mother of Emperor Daizong was Empress Dowager Zhangjing Wu. They first entered the princely household as consorts and were soon confined in the inner palace. Once enlightened rulers succeeded to the throne, honored titles were posthumously conferred upon them.

sentences.zh: 伏以魯國夫人發祥沙麓，貽慶河洲。

translations.literal: We respectfully note that the Lady of the State of Lu received her auspicious origin at Shalu and bequeathed her blessing at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully note that the Lady of Lu received her auspicious origin at Shalu and bequeathed her blessing at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 三後最賢，周母允成於天統；

translations.literal: Of the three queens, the most worthy—the mother of Zhou—fulfilled the mandate of heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Of the three queens, the most worthy—the mother of Zhou—fulfilled the mandate of heaven;

sentences.zh: 四妃有子，唐宮先啟於帝基，仰惟當寧之情，彌軫寒泉之思。

translations.literal: Of the four consorts who bore sons, the Tang palace first opened the imperial foundation. Looking up to the feelings of the ruler on the throne, we ever more feel the longing expressed in the Cold Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Of the four consorts who bore sons, the Tang palace first laid the imperial foundation. Reflecting the ruler's feelings on the throne, we feel ever more deeply the longing expressed in the Cold Spring.

sentences.zh: 久虛殷薦，慮損皇猷。

translations.literal: For long the solemn offerings have been neglected, and we fear this damages the imperial design.
translations.idiomatic: For long the solemn offerings have been neglected, and we fear this damages the imperial design.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹上尊諡曰宣憲皇太后，請依昭成皇太后故事，擇日備禮冊命。

translations.literal: Your servants respectfully submit the posthumous honorific title Empress Dowager Xuanxian and request that, following the precedent of Empress Dowager Zhaocheng, a day be chosen and the full rites of enfeoffment be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully submit the posthumous honorific title Empress Dowager Xuanxian and request that, following the precedent of Empress Dowager Zhaocheng, a day be chosen and the full rites of enfeoffment be prepared.

sentences.zh: 又，臣等伏聞先太后舊陵未祔先祠，則都下難崇別廟，既追尊諡，合創宮。

translations.literal: Furthermore, your servants have heard that the former empress dowager's old tomb has not been enshrined with the ancestral temple, so at the capital it would be difficult to establish a separate temple. Since a posthumous title is being pursued, a palace should be established.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, we have heard that the former empress dowager's tomb has not been enshrined with the ancestral temple, so at the capital it would be difficult to establish a separate temple. Since a posthumous title is being pursued, a memorial palace should be established.

sentences.zh: 按漢朝故事，園寢不在王畿，或就陵所便立寢祠。

translations.literal: According to Han dynasty precedent, park-tombs were not in the royal domain, or a tomb-shrine might conveniently be established at the burial site.
translations.idiomatic: According to Han dynasty precedent, park-tombs were not in the royal domain, or a tomb-shrine might conveniently be established at the burial site.

sentences.zh: 今商量上諡後，權立同廟，以申告獻，配祠之禮，請俟他年。」

translations.literal: Now, after deliberation, following the posthumous enfeoffment, a shared temple should provisionally be established to perform the rites of announcement and offering. The rites of joint enshrinement should be deferred to a later year."
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation, we propose that following the posthumous enfeoffment a shared temple be provisionally established to perform the rites of announcement and offering, while the rites of joint enshrinement should be deferred to a later year."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 據《歐陽史》云：議建陵寢，而太原石敬瑭反，乃於京師河南府東立寢宮。

translations.literal: According to the 《History of Ouyang》, it says: They deliberated on building a tomb-palace, but when Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan, they instead established a tomb-palace east of the capital in Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of Ouyang》 records that they deliberated on building a tomb-palace, but when Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan, they instead established a tomb-palace east of the capital in Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又案：《五代會要》所載明宗時內職，德妃王氏，天成三年正月冊立，長興二年四月進號淑妃，應順元年閏正月十三日冊為太妃，至周廣順元年四月追諡賢妃。

translations.literal: Further examining: The inner palace offices recorded in the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 under Emperor Mingzong include Virtuous Consort Wang, enfeoffed in the first month of the third year of Tiancheng, advanced to Pure Consort in the fourth month of the second year of Changxing, enfeoffed as Grand Consort on the thirteenth day of the intercalary first month of the first year of Yingshun, and posthumously honored as Worthy Consort in the fourth month of the first year of Guangshun under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 also lists inner palace offices under Mingzong: Virtuous Consort Wang, enfeoffed in the first month of Tiancheng 3, advanced to pure consort in the fourth month of Changxing 2, enfeoffed as grand consort on the thirteenth day of the intercalary first month of Yingshun 1, and posthumously honored as worthy consort in the fourth month of Guangshun 1 under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 昭儀王氏封齊國夫人，昭容葛氏封周國夫人，昭媛劉氏封趙國夫人，孫氏封楚國夫人，禦正張氏封曹國夫人，司寶郭氏封魏國夫人，司讚於氏封鄭國夫人，尚服王氏封衛國夫人，司記崔氏封蔡國夫人，司膳翟氏封滕國夫人，司醞吳氏封莒國夫人，婕妤高氏封渤海郡夫人，美人沈氏封太原郡夫人，順禦朱氏封吳郡夫人，司飾聊氏封潁川郡夫人，司衣劉氏封彭城郡夫人，司藥孟氏封咸陽郡夫人，梳篦張氏封清河郡夫人，司服王氏封太原郡夫人，櫛篦傅氏封潁川郡夫人，知客張氏賜號尚書，故江氏追封濟陽郡夫人。

translations.literal: Palace Lady of Bright Deportment Wang was enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Qi; Palace Lady of Bright Countenance Ge as Lady of the State of Zhou; Palace Lady of Bright Charm Liu as Lady of the State of Zhao; Sun as Lady of the State of Chu; Palace Lady of Correct Deportment Zhang as Lady of the State of Cao; Palace Keeper Guo as Lady of the State of Wei; Palace Commendation Yu as Lady of the State of Zheng; Director of Imperial Garments Wang as Lady of the State of Wei; Palace Recorder Cui as Lady of the State of Cai; Palace Provisioner Zhai as Lady of the State of Teng; Palace Brewer Wu as Lady of the State of Ju; Talented Lady Gao as Lady of Bohai Commandery; Beautiful Lady Shen as Lady of Taiyuan Commandery; Palace Lady of Correct Attendance Zhu as Lady of Wu Commandery; Palace Lady of Adornment Liao as Lady of Yingchuan Commandery; Palace Lady of Garments Liu as Lady of Pengcheng Commandery; Palace Lady of Medicine Meng as Lady of Xianyang Commandery; Palace Lady of Combs and Mirrors Zhang as Lady of Qinghe Commandery; Palace Lady of Garments Wang as Lady of Taiyuan Commandery; Palace Lady of Combs and Mirrors Fu as Lady of Yingchuan Commandery; Palace Hostess Zhang was granted the title Director; the late Lady Jiang was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Jiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Lady of Bright Deportment Wang was enfeoffed as Lady of Qi; Palace Lady of Bright Countenance Ge as Lady of Zhou; Palace Lady of Bright Charm Liu as Lady of Zhao; Sun as Lady of Chu; Palace Lady of Correct Deportment Zhang as Lady of Cao; Palace Keeper Guo as Lady of Wei; Palace Commendation Yu as Lady of Zheng; Director of Imperial Garments Wang as Lady of Wei; Palace Recorder Cui as Lady of Cai; Palace Provisioner Zhai as Lady of Teng; Palace Brewer Wu as Lady of Ju; Talented Lady Gao as Lady of Bohai Commandery; Beautiful Lady Shen as Lady of Taiyuan Commandery; Palace Lady of Correct Attendance Zhu as Lady of Wu Commandery; Palace Lady of Adornment Liao as Lady of Yingchuan Commandery; Palace Lady of Garments Liu as Lady of Pengcheng Commandery; Palace Lady of Medicine Meng as Lady of Xianyang Commandery; Palace Lady of Combs and Mirrors Zhang as Lady of Qinghe Commandery; Palace Lady of Garments Wang as Lady of Taiyuan Commandery; Palace Lady of Combs and Mirrors Fu as Lady of Yingchuan Commandery; Palace Hostess Zhang was granted the title Director; the late Lady Jiang was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Jiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以上皆長興三年九月敕。

translations.literal: All of the above were by edict in the ninth month of the third year of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above were by edict in the ninth month of Changxing 3.

sentences.zh: 其名號皆中書門下按《六典》內職仿而行之。

translations.literal: Their titles were all modeled by the Secretariat and Chancellery after the inner palace offices in the 《Six Canons》.
translations.idiomatic: Their titles were all modeled by the Secretariat and Chancellery after the inner palace offices in the 《Six Canons》.

sentences.zh: 內人李氏封隴西縣君，崔氏封清河縣君，李氏封成紀縣君，田氏封咸陽縣君，白氏封南陽縣君，並長興四年二月敕。

translations.literal: Inner palace woman Li was enfeoffed as Lady of Longxi County; Cui as Lady of Qinghe County; Li as Lady of Chengji County; Tian as Lady of Xianyang County; Bai as Lady of Nanyang County—all by edict in the second month of the fourth year of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: Inner palace woman Li was enfeoffed as Lady of Longxi County; Cui as Lady of Qinghe County; Li as Lady of Chengji County; Tian as Lady of Xianyang County; Bai as Lady of Nanyang County—all by edict in the second month of Changxing 4.

sentences.zh: 前代內職，皆無封君之禮，此一時之制。）〉

translations.literal: Inner palace offices of former ages had no rite of enfeoffing ladies. This was an institution of the moment.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Inner palace offices of former ages had no rite of enfeoffing ladies as county mistresses. This was an institution of the moment.)〉

sentences.zh: 閔帝哀皇后孔氏。

translations.literal: Empress Ai Kong of the Min Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ai Kong, consort of the Min Emperor.

sentences.zh: （案：《孔後傳》，原本闕佚。

translations.literal: (Note: The biography of Empress Kong is missing from the original text.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Empress Kong is missing from the original text.

sentences.zh: 據《通鑒》云：孔循陰遣人結王德妃，求納其女；

translations.literal: According to the 《Comprehensive Mirror》, it says: Kong Xun secretly sent men to ally with Virtuous Consort Wang, seeking to have his daughter received;
translations.idiomatic: The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 records that Kong Xun secretly sent men to ally with Virtuous Consort Wang, seeking to have his daughter received;

sentences.zh: 德妃請娶循女為從厚妃，帝許之。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Wang requested that Xun's daughter be taken as consort to Conghou, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Wang asked that Xun's daughter be taken as Conghou's consort, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，皇子從厚納孔循女為妃。

translations.literal: On gengyin day the prince Conghou received Kong Xun's daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Prince Conghou received Kong Xun's daughter as his consort.

sentences.zh: 《五代會要》云：初封魯國夫人，應順元年四月，為末帝所害。

translations.literal: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 says: She was first enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Lu. In the fourth month of the first year of Yingshun she was killed by the Last Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 records that she was first enfeoffed as Lady of Lu and was killed by the Last Emperor in the fourth month of Yingshun 1.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年正月二十八日，追諡為哀皇后。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the first month of the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin she was posthumously honored as Empress Ai.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the first month of Tianfu 5 she was posthumously honored as Empress Ai.

sentences.zh: 末帝劉皇后，應州人也。

translations.literal: Empress Liu of the Last Emperor was a native of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu of the Last Emperor was a native of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天成中，封為沛國夫人。

translations.literal: During the Tiancheng era, she was enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era, she was enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Pei.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，百官三上表，請立中宮，遂立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, the hundred officials submitted memorials three times requesting the establishment of the central palace, and she was thereupon made empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qingtai, officials submitted memorials three times requesting that an empress be installed, and she was thereupon made empress.

sentences.zh: 後性強戾，末帝甚憚之，故其弟延皓，自鳳翔牙校環歲之間曆樞密使，出為鄴都留守，皆由後內政之力也。

translations.literal: The empress's nature was fierce and obstinate, and the Last Emperor greatly feared her. Therefore her younger brother Yanhao, from a garrison officer at Fengxiang, within the space of a year passed through the office of Commissioner of Palace Affairs and went out as military governor of Ye— all through the empress's influence in inner governance.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was fierce and obstinate, and the Last Emperor greatly feared her. Her younger brother Yanhao rose from a garrison officer at Fengxiang to commissioner of palace affairs and then military governor of Ye within a single year—all through the empress's influence at court.

sentences.zh: 及延皓為張令昭所逐，執政請行朝典，後力製之，止從罷免而已。

translations.literal: When Yanhao was driven out by Zhang Lingzhao, the chief ministers requested that court law be applied. The empress forcibly blocked it, and he was merely dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanhao was driven out by Zhang Lingzhao, the chief ministers requested that court law be applied. The empress forcibly blocked it, and he was merely dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入洛。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor of Jin entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後與末帝俱就燔焉。

translations.literal: The empress and the Last Emperor both perished by fire.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and the Last Emperor both perished by fire.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔三代之興亡，雖由於帝王，亦係於妃後。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In antiquity the rise and fall of the Three Dynasties, though due to the emperors, were also tied to consorts and empresses.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: In antiquity the rise and fall of the Three Dynasties, though owing to the emperors, were also tied to consorts and empresses.

sentences.zh: 故夏之興也以塗山，及其亡也以妹嬉；

translations.literal: Thus Xia rose because of Tushan, and when it perished, because of Moxi;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xia rose because of Tushan, and when it fell, because of Moxi;

sentences.zh: 商之興也以簡狄，及其亡民以妲己；

translations.literal: Shang rose because of Jiandi, and when it perished, because of Daji;
translations.idiomatic: Shang rose because of Jiandi, and when it fell, because of Daji;

sentences.zh: 周之興也以文母，及其亡也以褒姒。

translations.literal: Zhou rose because of Queen Wen, and when it perished, because of Baosi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou rose because of Queen Wen, and when it fell, because of Baosi.

sentences.zh: 觀夫貞簡之為人也，雖未偕於前代，亦無虧於懿範。

translations.literal: Observing Lady Zhenjian as a person, though not equal to those of former ages, she in no way fell short of excellent example.
translations.idiomatic: As for Lady Zhenjian, though she cannot be ranked with the great consorts of antiquity, she in no way fell short of exemplary virtue.

sentences.zh: 而劉後以牝雞之晨，皇業斯墜，則與夫三代之興亡同矣。

translations.literal: But Empress Liu, with a hen crowing at dawn, caused the imperial enterprise to fall—then she was the same as the rise and fall of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: But Empress Liu, like a hen crowing at dawn, brought down the imperial enterprise—and in this she resembled the rise and fall of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 餘無進賢輔佐之德，又何足以道哉！

translations.literal: The rest had no virtue of advancing the worthy and assisting [the ruler]; how could they be worth mentioning!
translations.idiomatic: The rest had no virtue of advancing the worthy and assisting the ruler. What more is there to say of them!

sentences.zh: 〈（案：《五代史》無《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: (Note: The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 has no Biographies of Imperial Relatives.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 has no Biographies of Imperial Relatives.

sentences.zh: 據《五代會要》，武皇長女瓊華長公主，降孟知祥，同光三年十二月封。

translations.literal: According to the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》, the Martial Emperor's eldest daughter, Princess Chang of Qionghua, was married to Meng Zhixiang and enfeoffed in the twelfth month of the third year of Tongguang.
translations.idiomatic: According to the 《Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties》, the Martial Emperor's eldest daughter, Princess Chang of Qionghua, was married to Meng Zhixiang and enfeoffed in the twelfth month of Tongguang 3.

sentences.zh: 第二女瑤英長公主，降張延釗，同光三年十二月封。

translations.literal: The second daughter, Princess Chang of Yaoying, was married to Zhang Yanzhao and enfeoffed in the twelfth month of the third year of Tongguang.
translations.idiomatic: The second daughter, Princess Chang of Yaoying, was married to Zhang Yanzhao and enfeoffed in the twelfth month of Tongguang 3.

sentences.zh: 明宗長女永寧公主，降晉高祖。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong's eldest daughter, Princess Yongning, was married to the Founding Emperor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong's eldest daughter, Princess Yongning, was married to Gaozu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 第十三女興平公主，降趙延壽，天成三年四月封，至長興四年九月改封齊國公主，至清泰三年二月進封燕國長公主。

translations.literal: The thirteenth daughter, Princess Xingping, was married to Zhao Yanshou, enfeoffed in the fourth month of the third year of Tiancheng, changed to Princess of Qi in the ninth month of the fourth year of Changxing, and advanced to Princess Chang of Yan in the second month of the third year of Qingtai.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteenth daughter, Princess Xingping, was married to Zhao Yanshou, enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tiancheng 3, changed to Princess of Qi in the ninth month of Changxing 4, and advanced to Princess Chang of Yan in the second month of Qingtai 3.

sentences.zh: 第十四女壽安公主，長興四年六月封。

translations.literal: The fourteenth daughter, Princess Shou'an, was enfeoffed in the sixth month of the fourth year of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: The fourteenth daughter, Princess Shou'an, was enfeoffed in the sixth month of Changxing 4.

sentences.zh: 第十五女永樂公主，長興四年六月封。

translations.literal: The fifteenth daughter, Princess Yongle, was enfeoffed in the sixth month of the fourth year of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: The fifteenth daughter, Princess Yongle, was enfeoffed in the sixth month of Changxing 4.

sentences.zh: 今考《會要》所載，亦多舛互，如瓊華公主，《十國春秋》諸書作太祖弟克讓之女，《會要》以為武皇長女，此傳聞之異辭也。

translations.literal: Now examining what the 《Institutional Essentials》 records, there are also many discrepancies. For example, Princess Qionghua—in various books of the 《Spring and Autumn of the Ten States》 she is treated as the daughter of the Founding Emperor's younger brother Ke Rang, while the 《Institutional Essentials》 treats her as the Martial Emperor's eldest daughter. These are differing accounts from hearsay.
translations.idiomatic: Examining what the 《Institutional Essentials》 records, there are also many discrepancies. For example, Princess Qionghua—in various books of the 《Spring and Autumn of the Ten States》 she is treated as the daughter of the Founding Emperor's younger brother Ke Rang, while the 《Institutional Essentials》 treats her as the Martial Emperor's eldest daughter. These are differing hearsay accounts.

sentences.zh: 莊宗女義寧公主，降宋廷浩。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong's daughter, Princess Yining, was married to Song Tinghao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong's daughter, Princess Yining, was married to Song Tinghao.

sentences.zh: 廷浩仕至房州刺史，晉初為汜水關使，張從賓之叛，戰死。

translations.literal: Tinghao served as prefect of Fang Prefecture; in the early Jin era he was commissioner of Sishui Pass; when Zhang Congbin rebelled, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghao served as prefect of Fangzhou; in the early Jin era he was commissioner of Sishui Pass; when Zhang Congbin rebelled, he died in battle.

sentences.zh: 見《東都事略》及《宋史》。

translations.literal: See the 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》 and the 《History of Song》.
translations.idiomatic: See the 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》 and the 《History of Song》.

sentences.zh: 又，王禹偁《小畜集》有《宋渥神道碑》云：母義寧公主，天福中，晉祖以嘗事莊宗，有舊君之禮，每貴主入見，聽其不拜。

translations.literal: Further, Wang Yucheng's 《Collected Writings of Lesser Livestock》 contains the 《Spirit Way Stele of Song Wo》, which says: His mother was Princess Yining. In the Tianfu era, the Founding Emperor of Jin, because he had once served Emperor Zhuangzong, accorded her the courtesy due a former lord's consort; whenever the honored princess entered for audience, she was permitted not to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Further, Wang Yucheng's 《Collected Writings of Lesser Livestock》 contains the 《Spirit Way Stele of Song Wo》, which says that his mother was Princess Yining. During the Tianfu era, Gaozu of Jin, because he had once served Zhuangzong, accorded her the courtesy due a former lord's consort; whenever the honored princess came for audience, she was permitted not to bow.

sentences.zh: 時兵戎方熾，經費不充，惟公主之家，賜予甚厚，盡而復取，亦無倦色。

translations.literal: At that time warfare was raging and funds were insufficient; only the princess's household received lavish grants, and when they were exhausted they were replenished again—yet she showed no weariness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time warfare was raging and funds were insufficient; only the princess's household received lavish grants, and when they were exhausted they were replenished again—yet she showed no weariness.

sentences.zh: 一日，晉祖從容謂貴主曰：「朕於主家無所愛惜，但朝廷多事，府庫甚虛，主所知矣。

translations.literal: One day the Founding Emperor of Jin said calmly to the honored princess, "I hold nothing back from Your Highness's household, but the court has many affairs and the treasury is very depleted, as Your Highness knows.
translations.idiomatic: One day Gaozu of Jin said calmly to the honored princess, "I hold nothing back from Your Highness's household, but the court has many affairs and the treasury is very depleted, as Your Highness knows.

sentences.zh: 《會要》不載莊宗女，是其闕略也。

translations.idiomatic: The 《Institutional Essentials》 does not record Zhuangzong's daughters; this is one of its omissions.
